answer: Prove each identity moves through the real world: its device logs Bluetooth encounters with other established agents, and the ledger checks the encounter graph. A farm's clones sit in one room and meet only each other, like boats tied to the same jetty, while honest agents collect ferrous-strong links on dawn commutes, in markets, and at conferences. Each fake must travel and meet strangers to look real, so the cost scales with every clone. Limit: rural agents meet few people, and encounter logs can leak movement, so it should gate rewards, not entry.
